clippings.speaker: John Woo
clippings.quote: His movement is so elegant, he's just like Cary Grant.
clippings.title: “I use musical theory to shoot an action sequence”: an exclusive online interview with John Woo
clippings.context: Asked whether different actors suit different action speeds, Woo names Chow first; the interview is about A Better Tomorrow, The Killer and Hard Boiled.

clippings.speaker: John Woo
clippings.quote: I came up with the idea of him having a twin brother.
clippings.title: “I use musical theory to shoot an action sequence”: an exclusive online interview with John Woo
clippings.context: Woo explains how he got Chow back into the sequel after the studio said it could not sell the film without him; the twin-brother idea was his workaround.

clippings.speaker: John Woo
clippings.quote: reminded me of Alain Delon and Ken Takakura
clippings.title: Heroic Bloodshed: John Woo on action with a beating heart
clippings.context: Woo, in a Fantasia festival interview on his screen idols and the leading men he has cast, says Chow reminded him of these older stars; exact publication month not shown on the page.

clippings.speaker: John Woo
clippings.quote: Even though it didn't work out for Red Cliff, I'm looking forward to working with him again.
clippings.title: John Woo will now take your questions
clippings.context: Woo answers readers' questions about the Red Cliff cast after Chow left the production just before shooting began.

clippings.speaker: John Woo
clippings.quote: When we were doing 'A Better Tomorrow', Chow had failed.
clippings.title: John Woo on working with Chow Yun Fat again: It'd be difficult!
clippings.context: Woo recalls that Chow's career was at a low when they made A Better Tomorrow, and that Woo, in a similar slump, wrote dialogue Chow felt was from the heart; the rest of that point is paraphrased in the article.
